 Early voting surges as the midterm election approaches, signaling higher engagement and eagerness for Americans to make their voices heard.
 Advertisement Updated: 4:52 AM PST Nov 2, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Rachel Hirschheimer Washington Correspondent What does this year's record early voter turnout mean for the 2026 midterm elections?
 Early voting surges as the midterm election approaches, signaling higher engagement and eagerness for Americans to make their voices heard.
 Updated: 4:52 AM PST Nov 2, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Rachel Hirschheimer Washington Correspondent WASHINGTON — The midterm elections are less than 24 hours away, with all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats on the ballot as candidates make their final pitches to voters. 
 Historically, midterm elections have been challenging for the president's party, and Republicans may face difficulties maintaining control of both chambers. 
 Advertisement On Sunday, President Donald Trump returned to the campaign trail after hosting tele-rallies on Saturday. He visited Kansas and Iowa, where Senate races in these reliably Republican states are considered "toss-ups," according to the Cook Political Report . The nonpartisan organization also predicts Senate races in Ohio, Alaska, and Maine could go either way. 
 This year, early voting has shattered records, with the University of Florida Election Lab reporting that more than 54 million people have already cast advance ballots, nearly 9 million more than in the previous midterms. Nationally, 43% of these early votes cast were from registered Democrats, while 32% were from registered Republicans. However, the data is only available in 27 states, and the numbers don't tell us who people voted for this election cycle. 
 Political experts say this surge in early voting reflects heightened engagement among voters. 
 "Typically, people vote when they think their vote matters. If they think there are big issues on the ballot, and if they cast their ballot, they could help shape the outcome. That is when you get record turnouts," said Darrell West, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution . 
 Trump is scheduled to deliver a closing midterm pitch this afternoon at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, D.C., less than 24 hours before polls open.
